text:
The Senators are 16-7-3, 7-1-2 in their last ten, and the underlying numbers back it up. They own 52.7% of expected goals (the quality of chances each side gets) and 55% at five on five, and our playoff odds have them at 91% with a 28% shot at the division. This is not a team leaning on luck. Goals for and against both sit within three of what the chances predict.

The headlines tell you what kind of season it is. GM Steve Staios was in Nashville watching the Penguins, and Elliotte Friedman reported Ottawa's interest in Bryan Rust and Rickard Rakell, per a post by Graeme Nichols. A team that thinks it can win now is shopping. Meanwhile Tyler Boucher, son of former NHL goalie Brian Boucher, made his NHL debut, and Tim Stutzle has been on a point streak while getting written up as a player the league should notice.

The depth is the strength. Claude Giroux, Michael Amadio and Ridly Greig have taken 73% of the chances together, and Dylan Cozens has six goals and 12 points in his last 13. Thomas Chabot and Jordan Spence are 19-9 in goals at five on five. Linus Ullmark is on a heater (.929 over his last five), and Yahoo Sports argues Ottawa should manage his workload. The question for the next month is the one the Sens Nation Podcast raised this week: the backup, and what happens on the nights Ullmark doesn't start.
headline: Ottawa is good, and the market knows it
